findings.source_quote: τοῖς δὲ προλαβοῦσιν ὅτι θυσιῶν ὀρέγεται ὁ θεός
findings.english_quote: To those who had asserted beforehand that God desires sacrifices
findings.issue: προλαβοῦσιν here describes taking a position or forming an assumption beforehand. Unlike the preceding διαβεβαιουμένοις, it does not establish a confident verbal assertion. “Asserted” introduces an act of speech that the supplied wording does not establish; the note’s appeal to the following ὅτι clause does not resolve this distinction.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “To those who had assumed beforehand that God desires sacrifices.” Revise the lexical note to explain the preconception sense and distinguish it from the preceding verb of confident assertion. The replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἔφη „ὁ θεὸς ἔλεος θέλει καὶ οὐ θυσίας, ἐπίγνωσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐχ ὁλοκαυτώματα.
findings.english_quote: he said, “God wants mercy and not sacrifices, knowledge of him and not whole burnt offerings.”
findings.issue: The supplied text also lacks a closing quotation mark after the final quotation. The existing source_issues entry discloses the English closure after ἐστίν, but not this additional closure. The boundary is intelligible; this is an editorial-punctuation disclosure issue, not evidence of missing wording.
findings.suggested_revision: Extend source_issues to quote this final passage and disclose that the English supplies its closing quotation mark. Identify it as a punctuation feature of the supplied edition, without proposing lost words or requiring renewed print verification.

findings.issue: The masculine singular substantive ὁ ἀγαθός, reinforced by masculine εἷς, denotes the good one or the one who is good. English “the good” ordinarily denotes an abstraction or a collective class, obscuring the personal singular construction. The lexical note explains the choice but does not make that English formulation sufficiently clear.
findings.suggested_revision: Render “for the one who is good is one.” Preserve the unusual numerical predication rather than adding “God” or substituting a familiar canonical exclusion formula. Review the revised wording afresh.

findings.source_quote: μὴ ἐννοούμενον καὶ λέγοντα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἐλθεῖν καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς συνδούλους αὐτοῦ, ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων μετά τε πορνῶν καὶ μεθυόντων
findings.english_quote: Without taking thought, he says in his heart, ‘My lord is delaying his coming,’ and begins to beat his fellow servants, eating and drinking with both prostitutes and drunkards.
findings.issue: The draft turns accusative participles qualifying the appointed man into an independent affirmative continuation and renders subjunctive ἄρξηται as unqualified “begins.” A narrow scope for μή is a possible interpretation, so its existence alone is not a failure. Nevertheless, that scope does not itself justify the draft’s affirmative narrative or the loss of dependent/modal force. The note acknowledges the constructional shift and competing scopes but gives no contextual reason for choosing this main rendering.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the conduct within a qualification or warning rather than an unqualified affirmative sequel. One candidate for fresh review is: “… to give them their provisions at their proper time, without thinking and saying in his heart, ‘My lord is delaying his coming,’ and beginning to beat his fellow servants, eating and drinking with both prostitutes and drunkards.” Explain that this takes μή broadly over the coordinated conduct, fitting the characterization of the blessed appointee; preserve the narrower-scope alternative and explicitly disclose the shift to subjunctive ἄρξηται and nominative participles. Do not present the proposed revision as already accepted.
